thesis: Pre-open pack for 2026-09-29 is dominated by routine 8-K filings with no dated, decision-relevant single-name catalysts, plus soft-news items unrelated to markets. The two usable macro/market notes are: (1) Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson saying a possible S&P correction 'may be what the market needs' while favoring large-cap quality -- a cautious-but-not-bearish take that leans toward broad, quality-heavy exposure like VTI rather than away from equities; and (2) a calm risk backdrop (VIX 15.81, down ~1.6%; 10Y yield ticking down to 5.226%; oil/USO down 2-3%, disinflationary rather than alarming). Nothing here argues for de-risking or for chasing a specific headline-driven name, and per mandate I will not trade VIX/vol products, futures, or single-name biotech/SEC-filer noise. Book is currently ~85% cash (cash_usd 850.01 of 1000.12 equity) with only one small VTI sleeve (~15% of equity), well inside my 25% cash floor and 25%/4-position caps, and prior day-end continuity shows the group converging on modest VTI adds. Given a thin-but-benign pack, I'm proposing a small, non-aggressive continuation of the core VTI sleeve (+$50 notional) rather than a hold-only stance, since capital preservation is already amply satisfied by the large cash buffer and this size keeps VTI well under both my own 25% single-name cap and the shared book's 35% cap. No other new positions proposed; satellite ideas (Novo Nordisk licensing deal, TSMC site report, small-cap fund picks) are single-stock or thematic chatter without enough specificity or size discipline for a conservative sleeve and are being held for now, not acted on.
